findings.title: Webhook signature check fail-open when secret not configured
findings.issue: verifySignature() returned true when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET was blank, allowing unauthenticated webhook injection in production.
findings.fix: Added github.webhook.require-secret property (default false for local dev, set to true in prod via GITHUB_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_SECRET=true). When require-secret=true and no secret configured, returns 401 and logs ERROR.

findings.title: Unauthenticated admin endpoints (approve-bdd, refresh-context, pending-bdd)
findings.issue: POST /api/strategy/approve-bdd and POST /api/strategy/refresh-context were fully unauthenticated, allowing any caller to trigger compute-intensive codegen or git clone operations.
findings.fix: Added X-Admin-Key header guard backed by AIQA_ADMIN_KEY env var. Open mode when key not set (local dev warning logged). All three admin endpoints now protected.

findings.title: Actuator endpoints unrestricted — heapdump/env/beans potentially exposed
findings.issue: No management.endpoints.web.exposure.include configuration — Spring Boot default could expose env, beans, configprops, heapdump endpoints in production.
findings.fix: Added management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info and endpoint.health.show-details: never to all 5 service application.yaml files.

findings.title: Internal exception message leaked in webhook HTTP response
findings.issue: catch block returned e.getMessage() directly in the response body, potentially leaking internal class names, file paths, or stack trace fragments.
findings.fix: Replaced with generic 'Webhook processing failed' message. Full exception still logged internally at ERROR level.

findings.title: Temp file containing AI prompt accessible to other OS users
findings.issue: Temp file with AI prompt (may include code diffs) created with default umask permissions (world-readable on some systems).

findings.title: No request size limits for unbounded rawDiffContent
findings.issue: pr-service accepted unbounded POST body size. A large diff payload could cause memory exhaustion (OOM DoS).

noIssuesFound: No credentials hardcoded in source files
No tokens or API keys in log statements
Clone URL with embedded token (buildCloneUrl) NOT logged — props.getUrl() (clean URL) is logged instead
ProcessBuilder uses List<String> (not shell string) — no shell injection risk
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 always set — no interactive prompt hang risk
MessageDigest.isEqual() used for HMAC comparison — constant-time, safe from timing attacks
docker-compose.prod.yml uses ${VAR:-} placeholders — no hardcoded secrets
Redis keys use qa:pr: prefix — no sensitive data stored as values
Kafka consumers log raw message first, then deserialise — no credential content in diff messages

openRecommendations.title: Add OWASP Dependency Check to CI
openRecommendations.action: Add mvn dependency-check:check -Powasp to _service-build.yml. Fail on CVSS >= 7.

openRecommendations.title: Add security response headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options)
openRecommendations.action: Add spring-boot-starter-security with a no-auth SecurityFilterChain that only sets headers, or configure via server.tomcat.response-headers.

openRecommendations.title: Token in ProcessBuilder args (buildCloneUrl) — use GIT_ASKPASS instead
openRecommendations.action: Write token to a per-run script file (GIT_ASKPASS) instead of embedding in the clone URL arg. Reduces visibility in /proc/{pid}/cmdline for the brief clone process lifetime.
openRecommendations.status: OPEN — low risk (token not logged, process args visible only during git clone)
